chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Suleym al-Farra', from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to apply kohl with antimony when he went to his bed, once, once.
ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic practice regarding applying kohl before sleep?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Sulaym al-Farra’, highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) specific practice of applying ithmid (antimony) to each eye individually before sleep, a detail emphasized in Shia hadith literature for its medicinal and spiritual benefits. Scholars note that this 'odd' (witr) application aligns with the broader prophetic preference for odd numbers in acts of worship and hygiene, reflecting a holistic approach to physical well-being rooted in divine wisdom.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym Al Farra’a, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apply kohl with antimony (white powder) whenever he<sup>saww</sup> went to his<sup>saww</sup> bed, once, once (in each eye)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Salim al-Farra’ from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, applied al-Athmad (antimony) to his eyes before going to bed, once in each eye. 5 ”
